citation: Evolved Energy Research. EnergyPATHWAYS model and documentation. https://energypathways.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
description: EnergyPATHWAYS is Evolved Energy Research's accounting model for long-term energy-system transformations. It projects service demands, stocks of energy-consuming technologies and demand for fuels under explicit user choices about adoption, activity and technology retirement. Inputs are a CSV database, geographic mappings, demand drivers and scenario measures; outputs are large CSV tables of technology stocks, energy use, emissions and costs. Geography and model years follow the configured database. The current GitHub code is free under MIT terms and uses Python 3.10, the csvd package and an Excel interface. A command-line route is documented for Mac and Linux, while most development and testing uses Windows. An important limit is that the default stasis baseline assumes like-for-like technology replacement; alternative adoption paths must be specified as measures. It supports electricity, transport, building and industry transition studies. The separate archived energyPATHWAYS repository states that its older code was deprecated in 2020. The documentation was read, but no model or CSV database was downloaded or run. Geographic coverage follows the configured database. PyPSA (model-pypsa) is a related power-system planning model.
